checks.finding: Positive-capability matrix row 'G3: validator が正当な契約を誤検知しない' (acceptance-tests.md) cites 'AC-018 の境界正例' as proof that boundary pattern values `APIOrder`/`order-taking-2` are accepted, but AC-018's own AC-table Test Type is 'negative fixture (pattern 違反)' and its Test Target text defers the actual acceptance proof elsewhere: 'あわせて境界の正例として `APIOrder`（連続大文字）と `order-taking-2`（数字セグメント）が AC-003 の正例 fixture 系で受理されることを示し'. AC-003 — the only AC in this family typed 'positive fixture' — never names `APIOrder` or `order-taking-2` anywhere in its own Test Target text (which enumerates only Order/Fulfillment with purchase/delivery responsibilities and the 7 required + 3 optional fields). No AC whose Test Type is 'positive fixture' literally states these two boundary values pass. Downstream failure: a test author implementing TEST-003 from AC-003's text alone would not know to add these two fixtures, while a test author implementing TEST-018 would be adding a positive-acceptance assertion under a nominally negative-fixture test ID whose own text disclaims ownership of the proof. This violates the matrix's own accuracy rule ('AC の本文にフィールド名が現れないセルにこの記法を使ってはならない') and leaves no AC that a downstream verifier can point to as literally proving this declared capability. This is exactly the AC/TEST traceability the Positive-capability matrix exists to guarantee, so it belongs to spec review, not to design/task review. Major: missing observable acceptance criterion for a declared capability, not a workflow-safety contradiction.

No direct conflict found between requirements.md and acceptance-tests.md for the current round. Verified in both directions that all six REQ-005(a)-(f) fixture mandates are faithfully realized: AC-003 realizes (a) (Order=purchase only / Fulfillment=delivery only / mutual distinguished_from / Fulfillment.must_not_own=purchase price), AC-004 realizes (b) verbatim per this round's amendment ('REQ-005(b) の fixture 内容指定…をそのまま実現する'), AC-005 realizes (c), AC-006..AC-011 realize (d)'s six sub-items (d)-(i) one-for-one, AC-025 realizes (e), and AC-026 realizes (f) verbatim per this round's amendment, explicitly paired with AC-003 as REQ-005(f) itself requires ('(a) の全 populate 正例と対をなす'). Edge Cases, Non-goals, Roles and Permissions, and REQ-001..REQ-007 state no incompatible facts.

Every Edge Cases entry in requirements.md has a corresponding acceptance test: empty concepts[] -> AC-016; cross-context same-name concept (valid) vs. same-context same-name (invalid) -> AC-005 / AC-011; must_not_own absent -> AC-026; distinguished_from self-reference -> AC-008 ('自分自身への参照ケースを含む'); >10MB fail-closed input -> AC-017(2); v1 schema fed to v2 validator -> AC-012. Additional failure modes implied by REQ-002/003/004 (malformed JSON, type mismatch, minLength, minItems, pattern violation, dangling reference) are each covered by dedicated ACs (AC-014, AC-017(1), AC-018, AC-019, AC-020, AC-021, AC-022, AC-023, AC-024).

investigation.md's OQ-001..OQ-004 are each either resolved directly in requirements.md (OQ-003's essence-required proposal is adopted in REQ-002/Field Definitions, citing 'OQ-003 提案: required'; OQ-004's v1-rejection wording is adopted in REQ-004(b)/Edge Cases) or explicitly and narrowly deferred without blocking this feature's deliverables (OQ-001 v1-schema fate deferred to Phase 3 with Phase 0 staying 'no change'; OQ-002 CI/run-all registration deferred to a future WFI, with Phase 0 tests running via the existing unregistered-Pester convention per INV-007). requirements.md's own Assumptions section records the hook-fallback deviation and the v1-non-existence decision (INV-009) as settled facts, not open items requiring a design/task-time decision.

requirements.md explicitly scopes mechanical approval enforcement out of this feature: Non-goals states '`meta.status` の `Approved` 書込に対する機械的強制機構…の新設' is out of scope, and Roles and Permissions states 'v2 スキーマは `meta.status` を単なる列挙値フィールドとして定義するに留める' with '承認強制機構の新設は本 feature の非目標であり、必要と判断された場合は別 feature として起票する'. No AC tests approval-workflow semantics for meta.status — AC-021 only tests key presence, not value governance. No human-approval or irreversible-change boundary is in testable scope for Phase 0, so the explicit skip condition is met.

Aside from the traceability gap already recorded under AMBIGUITY, the specification hands off cleanly to implementation-policy review: Field Definitions enumerates every concept/term field with type, pattern, required-ness, and semantics; Roles and Permissions states editor/executor roles and the non-enforcement of the approval boundary explicitly; Main Workflows gives the 3-step usage loop; Edge Cases and Risks are populated with concrete mitigations tied to REQ-006's twin-parity and drift-lock tests. REQ-005(a)-(f) plus the Positive-/Negative-path matrices give an implementer a near-exhaustive fixture inventory without requiring invention of new product behavior.
